record.original_question: Find (or prove it does not exist) a complete hyperbolic manifold not biholomorphic to a convex domain where the Kobayashi and Carathéodory distances agree everywhere.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.5.5 Find (or prove it does not exist) a complete hyperbolic manifold not biholomorphic to a convex domain where the Kobayashi and Carathéodory distances agree everywhere. -M. Abate, abate@vaxsns.infn.it

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a connected complex manifold. The Kobayashi pseudodistance $k_M$ is the largest pseudodistance on $M$ for which every holomorphic map from the unit disc $\Delta \subset \mathbb{C}$ (equipped with the Poincaré distance $\omega$) to $M$ is distance-decreasing; equivalently, $k_M(p,q)$ is the infimum of $\sum_{i=1}^N \omega(z_i, w_i)$ over all chains of holomorphic discs $f_i:\Delta\to M$ with $f_1(z_1)=p$, $f_N(w_N)=q$, and $f_i(w_i)=f_{i+1}(z_{i+1})$. The Carathéodory pseudodistance is $c_M(p,q) = \sup\{\omega(f(p),f(q)) : f:M\to\Delta \text{ holomorphic}\}$. One has $c_M \le k_M$ in general. The manifold $M$ is called hyperbolic if $k_M$ is a distance, and complete hyperbolic if in addition $(M,k_M)$ is a complete metric space.

Determine whether there exists a complete hyperbolic complex manifold $M$, not biholomorphic to any convex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$, such that $c_M(p,q) = k_M(p,q)$ for every pair of points $p,q \in M$; or prove that no such manifold exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The open symmetrized bidisc $G_2 = \{(\lambda_1+\lambda_2, \lambda_1\lambda_2) : |\lambda_1|,|\lambda_2|<1\} \subset \mathbb{C}^2$ provides such an example. Agler–Young proved that the Carathéodory and Kobayashi distances coincide on $G_2$, while Costara (and others) showed that $G_2$ is not biholomorphic to any convex domain. As a bounded taut domain it is complete hyperbolic, so the problem is solved in the affirmative.

status_evidence.title: The symmetrized bidisc and Lempert's theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Carathéodory and Kobayashi distances coincide on the symmetrized bidisc, which is not biholomorphic to a convex domain.
status_evidence.claim: The symmetrized bidisc is a complete hyperbolic domain where c=k holds but which is not biholomorphic to any convex domain.

status_evidence.title: The Carathéodory and Kobayashi Metrics and Applications in Complex Analysis
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys results on equality of Carathéodory and Kobayashi distances, including the symmetrized bidisc example.
status_evidence.claim: The literature confirms the symmetrized bidisc as an example resolving Abate's problem.
